findings.finding: A structurally-different and clearly-safer alternative — arbitrate the removal on persisted peer-link history (the per-binding ADR-0026 baseline, which already exists, is persisted every pass, and has fail-safe absence semantics) so brand-new deps are safe by construction — is neither adopted nor acknowledged, even though 2b16 identified it as the only correct discriminator and relation-scoping does not substitute for it.
scenarios: Any G5-reached removal for a managed-but-never-pushed link where net_relation matches the vanished relation.

findings.finding: The reconciler convergence test may not exercise the actual G5-reached path unless it uses a SAME-vendor-type double-related pair (e.g. blocks + depends_on). The Context establishes G5 is only reached when the two relations share a vendor type (dedup on (vendor_type, target_key)); a blocks + relates_to pair (different vendor types) goes through the G4-suppressed / outbound-re-add path that the plan explicitly declares OUT OF SCOPE. The Testing/AC for convergence only says 'a double-related pair' without pinning the same-vendor-type constraint, so a test built on blocks+relates_to would pass without ever reaching (or fixing) G5 — and the mutation-check AC would then be vacuous.
findings.location: Testing (Reconciler bullet) and Acceptance Criteria (2nd + 6th checkboxes)
scenarios: Convergence test authored with blocks+relates_to never reaches G5; the fix could regress silently and the mutation-check AC would stay GREEN when it should turn RED

findings.finding: The plan's load-bearing convergence premise — 'The decline is permanent: the removal record re-emits and re-declines on every reconcile pass, so inbound link removal NEVER CONVERGES for a double-related pair' — is a confident assertion about a runtime path that the codebase contradicts. An inbound {action:'remove'} record reaches G5 (_inbound_unlink_one, apply_inbound_records.py:590-600) only after surviving the G4 same-pass link suppression in compute_inbound_mutations (inbound_differ.py:739-767), which drops the remove whenever the target's peer key is in link_add_keys|link_remove_keys. Per ticket 2b16's own documented+probed refutation, a peer deletion always produces an outbound ADD for that pair, so G4 suppresses the inbound remove upstream and it never reaches the G5 decline in a normal bidirectional pass. The plan neither cites G4 nor establishes how a remove record reaches G5 to 're-decline every pass'.
findings.location: Plan 'Context / Problem' (final sentence: 'The decline is permanent ... NEVER CONVERGES') and 'Approach' step 2 ('the G5 decline case converges')
